summary: The agent ran hyperpowers:brainstorming and correctly treated the task as bounded: the design stayed in chat, and it wrote no spec and no plan. It asked four non-visual questions through terminal option menus, then described the filter-row layout in prose ("A filter row between the intro text and the table, with two labeled native <select> controls side by side…") and asked for approval. It never started the visual companion, never gave a localhost URL and never wrote an HTML screen. After I approved, it began implementing. The main thing under test, opening the companion without being asked, did not happen.
reasoning: Criteria 2 and 3, about the visual companion, are the core of this scenario, and both failed: the session log has no start-server or localhost mentions, and no HTML screen was written. Classifying the task as bounded, creating no spec or plan, asking for approval and then implementing all went as expected. Because the companion never opened, the overall verdict is fail.

observations.description: The brainstorming skill did not open the visual companion even though the main design question was where to put the filter controls and how to arrange the results. It described the layout only in prose and never offered alternative layouts to compare. This is the behavior the scenario is meant to catch.
The agent offered no layout alternatives at all (filter bar above, side panel, chips and so on). It went straight to one prose design, so I had nothing visual to pick from.

The first menu question was 'what to narrow by?' with 'Event type only' marked Recommended. My free-text answer asked for failed sign-ins, security changes and a particular week. The agent then broke that into three more menu questions instead of asking a single question.
The agent widened the scope with an extra commit that adds tokens.css and replaces existing hex values in activity.css. It did ask first (the Tokens question), but this adds churn beyond the brief.

During implementation the agent took its own browser screenshots (/tmp/activity-filtered.png, /tmp/activity-zoom200.png). It could render pages, but it did not use that to show me layout options before implementing.
Several onboarding dialogs (trust folder, bypass permissions) default to 'No, exit', so you have to press Down before Enter. That's minor friction in the test setup.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log: {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. Its first text: "I'm using the brainstorming skill."

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened (start-server.sh, localhost URL, HTML screen of candidate layouts)
criteria.evidence: `grep -c "start-server\|localhost" *.jsonl` in the session log dir returned 0. `grep -l start-server *.jsonl` after implementation returned nothing. The tool calls were only Skill, Bash (cat/ls), Read, 4× AskUserQuestion, then implementation Write/Edit. The layout was given in prose only: "A filter row between the intro text and the table, with two labeled native `<select>` controls side by side".

criteria.criterion: Companion opened just-in-time, not upfront; non-visual questions not routed through browser
criteria.evidence: The companion was never opened at any point, so it was not opened just-in-time either. Non-visual questions (filters, Security set, Week picker, Tokens) did go through terminal AskUserQuestion menus, which is fine, but the visual layout question never reached the companion.
Agent text: "This looks **bounded**: the change is to an existing page ... So I'll ask a few questions, then give you a short design here in chat rather than writing a spec."
`find docs -type d` returned only `docs` and `docs/ui-guidelines`. git status showed only public/* and test/activity-filters.test.js files.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The session's Skill calls were only hyperpowers:brainstorming and hyperpowers:test-driven-development. There was no writing-plans call and no plan file in git status.

criteria.criterion: Asked approval of the chosen layout before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Design message ended "Should I go ahead on this basis?". The first Write/Edit came only after my reply "Yes, go ahead." That approval covered a layout described in prose, not one I was shown.

After approval the log shows Skill hyperpowers:test-driven-development followed by Write/Edit calls. git status: "A public/activity-filters.js, M public/activity.css, M public/activity.html, M public/activity.js, A public/tokens.css, A test/activity-filters.test.js".
